channel.description: Latest articles from Ink Free News (inkfreenews.com)

item.title: Lawmakers vote to dissolve hundreds of townships, sending bill to Braun
item.description: Hundreds of Indiana's township governments will eventually be dissolved under legislation that received final approval from the Indiana Senate, sending it to Gov. Mike Braun's desk.

item.title: Warsaw Teenager Arrested For Allegedly Threatening, Battering Two Women
item.description: A Warsaw teenager was recently arrested for allegedly threatening and battering two women.

item.title: Combined Community Services’ Love Thy Neighbor Luncheon Demonstrates Community Impact
item.description: Combined Community Services held their annual ‘Love thy neighbor' luncheon Thursday, Feb. 26.

item.title: Braun Urges Year-Round E15 Fuel Sales
item.description: Gov. Mike Braun is urging Indiana’s congressional delegation to back federal legislation allowing year-round sales of E15 gasoline, saying the change would support farmers and strengthen the rural economy.

item.title: Indiana Stadium Plan Won’t Move Bears Headquarters
item.description: The Chicago Bears confirmed Monday, Feb. 23 that the franchise will not relocate its headquarters or training operations to Indiana, even as discussions continue about building a new stadium in Hammond.

item.title: FCCF Highlights Nick Patterson Legacy Fund
item.description: On what would have been his 43rd birthday, the Fulton County Community Foundation is honoring the life and legacy of Sgt. Nicholas “Nick” James Patterson by sharing the story behind the Nick Patterson Legacy Fund: Serving Others, Honoring His Sacrifice.

item.title: Immigration Crackdown Heads To Governor After Falling Short Last Year
item.description: Indiana’s Senate on Wednesday, Feb. 25 sent a bill mandating local government cooperation with federal immigration detainer requests - and punishing businesses who employ unauthorized workers - to Gov. Mike Braun after consenting to edits in the House.

item.title: Supreme Court Tariff Reversal Creates Uncertainty For Indiana RV Industry
item.description: Indiana’s recreational vehicle industry is facing renewed uncertainty following a U.S. Supreme Court ruling that struck down emergency powers tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump, disrupting a newly negotiated trade agreement with Indonesia.

item.title: Indiana Senate Sends ‘Bell-To-Bell’ School Cellphone Ban To Governor
item.description: A proposal to keep cellphones out of Hoosier students’ hands for the entire school day is headed to the governor’s desk after clearing its final legislative hurdle Wednesday, Feb. 25.

item.title: The Jim Irsay Collection To Be Auctioned
item.description: More than 300 pieces from the late Jim Irsay’s vast pop culture collection are heading to auction next month, with estimates suggesting the most prized items could fetch up to $39.9 million.
